_comment: Maps each Vibe-IC flow step to the right Bucket-A program file + Bucket-B skill file. Used by enhancement_emit.py to route a captured recovery to the correct target. Step IDs match the canonical flow naming.

phase1.ingest_render.description: Phase 1: NL prompt / docs → L1-L27 JSON

phase1.fact_extract.description: Phase 1 ingester pattern matching on NL prose

phase2.rtl_gen.description: Phase 2: spec-to-RTL (the WAIVE → AI-author handoff path)
phase2.rtl_gen.bucket_A_related_note: `spec_declaration_emit.py` owns the FREE-CHOICE declaration contract at this step: the spec's own MUST-declare clause + field table decide which interface choices the author must record BEFORE authoring, and the emitter refuses (naming the field) rather than defaulting one. Route a recovery here whenever the recovered fact was a decision the designer made that no downstream tool could infer — bit order, reset-release latency, integer encoding, reset polarity, a build parameter, an optional-feature selection. Do NOT route such a recovery to a value-inference program: inferring a free choice from the artifacts is the defect, not the fix.
phase2.rtl_gen.ic_expert_db_note: A recovery that is generalizable DESIGN-CLASS CRAFT (algorithm correctness / interface convention / latency-reset discipline / a common trap) — but is NOT a deterministic rule a gate can enforce — is distilled as a chip-AGNOSTIC lesson into the IC Expert DB (keyed by ic_class). It ADVISES the general spec-to-rtl author via _lesson_digest (surfaced for any Phase-1 doc, not just benchmarks); it NEVER overrides a gate/program verdict. Enforce with ic_expert_db_consistency_check.py (blindness + no-override). This is the 4th distill target alongside program (Bucket A) / skill (Bucket B) / backlog (Bucket C).

phase2.rtl_gen.canonical_primitive.description: Phase 2 deterministic canonical-primitive recognition and RTL emission from a prompt-visible architecture

phase2.full_stack_tb.description: Full-stack testbench GENERATION (professional/self-checking TB authored around the DUT) — distinct from phase2.reference_tb which CHECKS a generated TB.

phase2.tb_substance.description: Functional-verification SUBSTANCE — does a generated testbench actually drive the DUT, or does it merely print a pass? Distinct from phase2.full_stack_tb (which GENERATES a TB) and phase2.reference_tb (which checks a generated TB RAN). Discovery must stay DIRECTORY+STRUCTURE driven: scenario-named TBs (case_3.v, corner_operand.v) match no tb_*.v / *_tb.v glob, so a filename-driven audit silently reports zero hits on a corpus of real defects.

phase2.pad_budget.description: Phase 2 step 2: can the declared interface be bonded out on a purchased slot at all (pad-budget arithmetic, fold candidates)

phase2.lec.description: LEC / logical-equivalence checking — RTL <-> synthesized (and post-layout) gate netlist. Covers hierarchy staging (a hard-macro staged on only ONE side makes hierarchy -check abort with compared_points: 0, which must NOT be booked as a real FAIL) and PASS-vs-report-verdict consistency (a step must not report PASS over a report whose json verdict is FAIL).

phase2.lec_execution.description: LEC producer execution and convergence: Yosys must be supervised by progress of its actual host/container process tree, preserve the declared total attempt budget, reap only the stamped invocation on stall/ceiling, and publish an honest no-verdict resource outcome rather than a design FAIL when execution cannot finish.

phase3.pad_ring.description: Pad-ring site resolution, per-side fit and abutment for the self-tape-out path (flow step 15.5ic). Routed to the step's GATE: flow/phase1_phase2_phase3.yaml declares 15.5ic's verdict as `program_exit_zero: pad_ring_check`, so a rule recovered here belongs in the checker; the producer and the shared helper are named as related. Added because the step had no routing entry at all, so a capture taken here fell through to default_routing, whose bucket_A_program is null.

phase3.floorplan.description: Floorplan / die-area / core-utilization / macro placement setup ahead of PnR.

phase3.pnr_setup_repair.description: PnR set_wire_rc + repair_design + repair_timing -setup (added in v0.1.26)

analog.A2_topology.description: Analog A2: per-block topology selection (SC integrator + comparator + DAC, etc.)

analog.A4_corner_sweep.description: Analog A4: real-ngspice corner sweep — template families per block-type (LDO, OTA, ADC, ΔΣ)

analog.sizing_loop._note: Bucket A target TBD — analog sizing loop currently has no single dedicated check program; the closest is the analog-sizing-loop skill itself. File a backlog if a deterministic sizing-loop checker is authored.

benchmark.scoring.description: Host scorers (score_iverilog_tb.py / score_cocotb_mcp.py) — cwd=design_dir, substitution disclosures, etc.

benchmark.verify_claim_done.description: benchmark-verify's final 'Plugin-test hard rule' (vibe-ic#1130). If a verification run modified plugin code, DONE may not be claimed until the FULL pytest suite -- BOTH programs/tests/ and tests/ -- has passed. The gate turns that conditional into a mechanical verdict; before this entry the rule existed only as prose in the skill, so it ran when an agent remembered and produced no verdict when one did not.

mcp_eda.cocotb.description: MCP eda_cocotb — sibling .py staging, PYTHONPATH, etc. (the CVDP harness_library lesson)

mcp_eda.synth.bucket_A_note: The MCP server is a SINGLE module: every eda_* tool is registered in mcp-eda/src/index.js. These three routes named mcp-eda/src/tools/{synth,lint,cocotb}.js, which have NEVER existed in this repository at any commit, so every MCP-EDA capture was routed to a file nobody could open and enhancement_emit.py wrote a rule sketch telling the reader to merge into it. The path check that should have caught this exempted every mcp-eda/ route on the false premise that mcp-eda is a sibling package; it ships inside the plugin. Shared helpers live in mcp-eda/src/lib/*.mjs.

phase3.die_finishing.description: Die finishing: the seal ring, driven through the PDK's own generator, and the die identification cells.

repo.absence_verdict.description: A refusal that a declared thing is not there. The rule this step carries: an absence verdict must name the search space it exhausted, because 'not found' and 'not looked for' are different verdicts that print the same way.

repo.upstream_parity.description: Where this plugin RE-IMPLEMENTS an upstream flow's computation or configuration contract
repo.upstream_parity._comment: Deliberately NOT routed to the step a divergence was first found at: the rule is about re-implementation, not about the subsystem that happened to surface it.

repo.pr_scope.description: Merge gate: which of the twenty Appendix-C review questions a change-set makes applicable, and whether each is backed by evidence a machine can re-verify

benchmark.aggregate_verdict.description: Aggregating many per-subject exit codes into one verdict for a corpus run

flow.artefact_write_ownership.description: Wiring a gate's output path against the artefact paths producers already write

repo.generated_manifest.description: Regenerating a tracked manifest whose subject is the tracked file set

repo.enforcement_point.description: Proving that a named client-side enforcement point is installed and current

repo.unique_lookup.description: Resolving an artefact a caller expects to be unique, when the search returns several

ppa.proof_group_equivalence.description: Admitting an alternative way to establish an axis alongside the original

repo.verdict_provenance.description: Emitting a verdict that will be quoted after the tree it judged has moved

repo.lane_artefact_namespace.description: Landing a document one lane owns, when another lane owns a document of the same kind

flow.matrix_d1_wiring.description: The 68x9 matrix's wiring dimension: does something real parse and execute each declared gate

flow.matrix_d2_falsifiable.description: The 68x9 matrix's falsifiability dimension: can each gate reach a genuine non-zero exit

flow.matrix_d3_outputs_produced.description: The 68x9 matrix's outputs dimension: are declared required_outputs genuinely written by a run

flow.matrix_d6_skip_discipline.description: The 68x9 matrix's skip dimension: is a skip conditioned on a runtime fact and reported at a non-PASS tier

publish.figure_agreement.description: A published page stating one named figure twice, with two different values

default_routing._comment: Fallback when a step has no entry above — used by enhancement_emit.py only as last resort. Bucket B catch-all is ic-expert-agent.md (general design judgment).
